```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggrepel)

df_raw <- read_csv("data/GlobalFindexDatabase2025.csv")

# Subset 1: country-level aggregates for 2024
df_all <- df_raw %>%
  filter(year == 2024, group2 == "all")

# Subset 2: gender breakdown for 2024
df_gender <- df_raw %>%
  filter(year == 2024, group == "gender")

# Subset 3: one row per country with gender gap computed
df_gap <- df_gender %>%
  select(
    countrynewwb, regionwb24_hi, incomegroupwb24,
    group2, account_t_d, mobileaccount_t_d, fiaccount_t_d
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = group2,
    values_from = c(account_t_d, mobileaccount_t_d, fiaccount_t_d)
  ) %>%
  mutate(gender_gap = account_t_d_men - account_t_d_women) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gender_gap))
```

## Overview

- **Question:** Does mobile money access help close the gender gap in financial inclusion?
- **Data:** World Bank Global Findex 2025 — 152 countries, 2024
- **Approach:** Descriptive analysis, covariation, and regression
- **Finding:** Mobile money is negatively associated with the gender gap,
  but the effect is modest and not statistically significant —
  suggesting broader structural barriers remain

## Data

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
\small
- **Source:** World Bank Global Findex 2025
- **Coverage:** 152 countries, 2024
- **Unit of analysis:** Country-level averages by gender
- **Key variables:**
  - *Account ownership:* share of adults with a financial account
  - *Mobile money:* share of adults with a mobile money account
  - *Gender gap:* men's minus women's account ownership rate
    (positive = men higher)
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r}
# Summary statistics table
df_gap %>%
  filter(!is.na(incomegroupwb24)) %>%
  summarise(
    `Mean ownership, men`   = mean(account_t_d_men,   na.rm = TRUE),
    `Mean ownership, women` = mean(account_t_d_women, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Mean gender gap`       = mean(gender_gap,        na.rm = TRUE),
    `Max gender gap`        = max(gender_gap,         na.rm = TRUE),
    `Min gender gap`        = min(gender_gap,         na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to  = "Statistic",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Value = scales::percent(Value, accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  kable(
    format   = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align    = c("l", "r")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 9, latex_options = "hold_position")
```
:::
::::

## Financial Inclusion Around the World

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
\small
- Account ownership varies dramatically across regions
- Middle East & North Africa shows the lowest median
- High-income countries cluster near full inclusion
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
```{r fig-region, fig.width=4.5, fig.asp=0.75}
# Clean region labels once and reuse
df_all_clean <- df_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(regionwb24_hi)) %>%
  mutate(
    regionwb24_hi = str_remove(
      regionwb24_hi, " \\(excluding high income\\)"
    )
  )

region_medians <- df_all_clean %>%
  group_by(regionwb24_hi) %>%
  summarize(med = median(account_t_d, na.rm = TRUE))

df_all_clean %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = fct_reorder(regionwb24_hi, account_t_d, median),
    y = account_t_d
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7, color = "gray30") +
  geom_text(
    data = region_medians,
    aes(
      x     = regionwb24_hi,
      y     = med,
      label = scales::percent(med, accuracy = 1)
    ),
    hjust = -0.2, size = 3, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x       = NULL,
    y       = "Account ownership (% of adults)",
    caption = "Source: World Bank Global Findex 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 5, b = 20, l = 5))
```
:::
::::

## Mobile Money and the Gender Gap

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
\small
- Countries with higher mobile money adoption show a smaller
  gender gap
- The negative trend is largely driven by Sub-Saharan Africa's
  high mobile money adoption
- Considerable variation around the trend suggests other factors
  are at play
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
```{r fig-scatter, fig.width=4, fig.asp=0.85}
# Clean region labels and identify outliers
df_gap_clean <- df_gap %>%
  filter(!is.na(mobileaccount_t_d_women), !is.na(regionwb24_hi)) %>%
  mutate(
    regionwb24_hi = str_remove(
      regionwb24_hi, " \\(excluding high income\\)"
    )
  )

outliers <- df_gap_clean %>%
  filter(
    mobileaccount_t_d_women > quantile(
      mobileaccount_t_d_women, 0.85, na.rm = TRUE
    ) |
    gender_gap > quantile(gender_gap, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE) |
    gender_gap < quantile(gender_gap, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

df_gap_clean %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x     = mobileaccount_t_d_women,
    y     = gender_gap,
    color = regionwb24_hi
  )) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 1.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm", se = FALSE,
    color = "gray30", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data      = outliers,
    aes(label = countrynewwb),
    size = 2, fontface = "bold", max.overlaps = 15
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x       = "Mobile money ownership, women (% adults)",
    y       = "Gender gap in account ownership",
    color   = NULL,
    caption = "Source: World Bank Global Findex 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.text     = element_text(size = 5),
  legend.key.size = unit(0.25, "cm")
) +
guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 3))
```
:::
::::

## Regression Analysis

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r fig-coef, fig.width=3.8, fig.asp=0.85, fig.cap=NULL}
# Fit model and build coefficient plot data
m1 <- lm(
  gender_gap ~ mobileaccount_t_d_women + incomegroupwb24,
  data = df_gap
)

coef_df <- coef(summary(m1)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Term") %>%
  filter(Term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    Term = case_when(
      Term == "mobileaccount_t_d_women"           ~ "Mobile money,\nwomen",
      Term == "incomegroupwb24Low income"          ~ "Low income",
      Term == "incomegroupwb24Lower middle income" ~ "Lower middle\nincome",
      Term == "incomegroupwb24Upper middle income" ~ "Upper middle\nincome"
    ),
    lower = Estimate - 1.96 * `Std. Error`,
    upper = Estimate + 1.96 * `Std. Error`
  )

ggplot(coef_df, aes(
  x = Estimate,
  y = fct_reorder(Term, Estimate)
)) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50"
  ) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    height = 0.2, color = "gray30"
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x       = "Coefficient estimate (95% CI)",
    y       = NULL,
    caption = "Source: World Bank Global Findex 2025"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
\small
- Mobile money shows a negative but marginally significant
  association (p = 0.089)
- Income group adds little explanatory power
- Structural barriers beyond income and mobile access
  likely drive the gap
:::
::::


## Conclusion

**Mobile money alone won't close the gender gap.**

- Account ownership gaps persist across most regions, even where
  mobile money is widespread
- Mobile money shows a negative but marginally significant
  association with the gender gap (p = 0.089)
- Structural barriers beyond income and mobile access —
  legal rights, education, social norms — likely drive the gap

*Future work: longitudinal analysis tracking how mobile money
expansion affects within-country gender gaps over time*
